figures.finding: A child who hasn't finished the school year in which he turns fifteen may not be employed or work in any capacity save light work; a child of fifteen up to the prescribed minimum age may do only light work that harms neither health nor schooling and meets any regulations; no one under eighteen may do hazardous work. School work under sixteen in an authorised programme is outside the rule.

value.general: end of the school year of the 15th birthday
value.lightWork: 15 to the prescribed minimum age, on conditions

sources.said: (1) A child who has not yet completed the calendar year of schooling in which he or she reaches the age of 15 years must not be employed or work in any capacity, except in light work as prescribed by section 43.

(1) A child aged at least 15 years but under the prescribed minimum age of employment in section 42 must not be employed or work in any capacity, except in light work that: (a) is unlikely to be harmful to the health and development of the child; (b) will not affect the child’s school or vocational training attendance;

figures.finding: Tuvalu's Act has no performer's rule: the bar on any work before the end of the school year of the fifteenth birthday covers performing, and light work from fifteen is on the Minister's regulations (hours and times), none of which were found; the employer keeps a register of every child employed (name, birth date, occupation, pay, dates). The rule is for any work, writing or directing included.
